No caller/provider enumerator or CopyTo participates.

These benign filters are not sent to the provider or sealed. Then snapshot real filters and invoke the original full Validate on the frozen actual request before deadline/source call. Failed snapshots retain invalid empty kinds for original invalid-filter refusal and safe invalid-request sealing.

After unchanged null/unavailable and cancellation handling, short-circuit bounded provider node/edge snapshots on failure, returning original Refused/source-budget. Only frozen projection lists reach original Validate/Seal. Filter snapshots also short-circuit after a prior snapshot failure, so later callbacks cannot mask the detected refusal.

Original deadline/caller-cancellation catch, default/explicit depth rules, stale identity status mapping, provider interface/default unavailable source, Empty and shared Validate/Seal implementations remain unchanged.

Catch only ArgumentOutOfRangeException and IndexOutOfRangeException from the indexed copy. Return snapshot failure only when a direct current Count read proves the failed captured index is absent (Count<=index); otherwise bare throw preserves that exception. Count proof is in the catch body, not an exception filter, so its arbitrary exceptions/cancellation propagate through original handling. No catch-all or new OCE catch.
sourceReviewLimits: Observed Count drift is rejected. This is a bounded ordinary snapshot, not a linearizable concurrency guarantee. Mutations that keep Count unchanged may affect which values are captured; all captured values still pass the original validator before use.

Arbitrary source.ReadAsync failures, initial/final Count getter errors, unproved/stable-count bounds failures and other indexer errors propagate, subject only to the unchanged original deadline OCE handling. Recognized indexed shrinkage alone becomes invalid-filter/source-budget Refused. Count proof getter failures also propagate; custom callbacks can still block or allocate internally and no preemption/qualification is asserted.
